description:
Ross Colton forever etched his name in Lightning history with his championship-clinching goal in Game 5 of the 2021 Stanley Cup Final. Midway through the second period, Colton found the perfect spot in front of the Canadiens' net. Defenseman David Savard delivered a brilliant pass through traffic, and Colton redirected it past Carey Price at 13:27 to break the deadlock.  
That single goal was all it took to secure a 1-0 victory and Tampa Bay's second consecutive Stanley Cup. Colton's timely finish made him just the second rookie in modern NHL history to score a Cup-winning goal, cementing his place in Bolts lore and sparking unforgettable celebrations on home ice.

description:
With 21 career hat tricks to his name, including two in the postseason, David Pastrnak has a knack for finding the back of the net. One particularly memorable performance came against the rival Montreal Canadiens in February 2020. Early in the first period, Pastrnak opened the scoring off a perfect feed from Brad Marchand. He struck again early in the second, finishing a two-on-one opportunity in style. To complete the hat trick, Pastrnak buried a rebound late in the second period, prompting a shower of hats from the ecstatic home crowd. That season, Pastrnak claimed the Maurice “Rocket” Richard Trophy as the League’s top goal-scorer, sharing the honor with Washington Capitals forward Alex Ovechkin with an impressive 48 goals.

description:
On April 15, 2024, Lucas Raymond delivered a clutch performance to keep the Red Wings' playoff hopes alive with a dramatic late-game goal in Detroit. Trailing 4–3 with under two minutes remaining in the third period, defenseman Shayne Gostisbehere made a key play by leaping to keep the puck inside the blue line, keeping the Red Wings’ attack alive. Raymond seized the moment, taking a pass from David Perron and firing a quick shot past Canadiens goaltender Sam Montembeault to tie the game with just 1:17 left on the clock.   Raymond would later step up again in overtime, scoring the game-winner.  
While the Red Wings ultimately missed the playoffs, Lucas Raymond’s late-game heroics were a bright spot in the final stretch of the season. His ability to deliver in high-pressure moments highlighted his poise and skill, marking a memorable night for the young star as he continued to show why he’s one of the brightest talents in Detroit’s future.

description:
Wyatt Johnston delivered a clutch performance for the Dallas Stars in Game 3 of the First Round of the 2024 Stanley Cup Playoffs, scoring the overtime winner to secure a 3-2 victory over the Vegas Golden Knights. With the series hanging in the balance and Dallas facing the threat of an 0-3 hole, Johnston stepped up late in overtime. Skating down the wing, he froze Logan Thompson with a quick move before roofing a sharp-angle shot into the top corner, sparking wild celebrations and ending a six-game losing streak against the defending champs.  
Johnston had already given the Stars an early lead, scoring in the first period, and finished the game with two goals and eight shots. His overtime heroics not only cut the series deficit to 2-1 but proved to be a turning point. Dallas went on to win the series in seven games, with Johnston’s big moment helping to reignite the team’s playoff run and solidifying the 20-year-old as one of the rising stars in the league.

description:
Artturi Lehkonen etched his name into Stanley Cup history with the championship-winning goal in Game 6 of the 2022 Final. With the game tied 1-1 midway through the second period, Lehkonen found himself in the right place at the right time. Nathan MacKinnon’s attempted pass deflected off a defender and landed on Lehkonen’s stick. Wasting no time, he fired a quick shot past Andrei Vasilevskiy at 12:28, giving the Avalanche a 2-1 lead they wouldn’t relinquish.  
Lehkonen’s opportunistic goal sealed Colorado’s first Stanley Cup in over two decades, capping off a playoff run where his clutch play and tireless effort were key to the Avalanche’s success. On a roster loaded with talent, Lehkonen’s ability to seize the moment ensured his place in Avs lore.

description:
In a thrilling, high-scoring Stadium Series matchup against their rival New York Islanders, the Rangers mounted a late comeback to tie the game. Mika Zibanejad delivered the equalizer late in the third period, sending the contest into overtime. In the extra frame, fresh off the center-ice faceoff, Artemi Panarin intercepted a pass attempt, dropping the puck right in front of the Islanders' net. Although his initial shot was stopped, Panarin pounced on the rebound and buried it, sealing the victory with a dramatic game-winning goal.

description:
Sidney Crosby, already celebrated as one of the NHL's all-time greats, continues to build on his legendary career. With his 24th goal of the season, Crosby reached 1,670 career points, surpassing Wayne Gretzky for fourth on the all-time list for points with a single franchise. The milestone highlights Crosby's consistency and dominance as the face of the Pittsburgh Penguins since his rookie season in 2005-06. From Stanley Cups to MVP awards, Crosby's achievements have solidified his place in hockey history, and this accomplishment further cements his status as a cornerstone of the Penguins’ franchise.

description:
Matvei Michkov made a statement in his rookie season, leading all rookies with 26 goals, including a League-best three in overtime. Playing at home in Philadelphia against the Chicago Blackhawks, Michkov showcased his instincts during a power play in the extra frame. Skating into the backdoor area, he received a pass from Travis Konecny and slammed it home for the game-winner. Not only did Michkov lead all NHL rookies in goals, but he also finished as the top goal scorer for the Philadelphia Flyers, solidifying his place as a key player for the team.

description:
Tage Thompson delivered an unforgettable performance, scoring five goals—matching the Buffalo Sabres' record for most goals in a game—including four in the first period, the second-fastest start with four goals in NHL history, as Buffalo dominated Columbus. Since arriving in 2018-19, Thompson has been the franchise’s top goal-scorer, hitting the 40-goal mark in two different seasons. The highlight showcases his incredible skill set, from soft hands around the net to a blistering one-timer and a wrist shot with pinpoint accuracy.

description:
Acquired in late March 2022 to bolster the Carolina Hurricanes’ playoff push, Max Domi delivered a standout performance in their Game 7 First Round victory over the Boston Bruins, scoring two crucial goals. Early in the second period, Domi battled for the puck in the corner, worked it back to the point, and drove to the net. There, he slammed in a loose puck at the side of the crease to give Carolina a 2-0 lead. Later in the period, after Boston cut the lead to one, Domi unleashed a one-timer from the high slot that found the back of the net, restoring the Hurricanes' two-goal cushion. His heroics helped secure the series-clinching win.

description:
On March 26, 2022, before a game against the New Jersey Devils, Nicklas Backstrom was honored for reaching the 1,000-point milestone earlier that season. The evening began with a heartfelt pregame ceremony, where Backstrom received tributes from teammates, coaches, and fellow NHL stars, recognizing his career achievement. 
In the game itself, Backstrom delivered a memorable performance, scoring the key go-ahead goal in the third period to break a 2-2 tie and help the Capitals secure a 4-3 victory. As the crowd roared in approval, fans celebrated the moment by showering the ice with thousands of foam apples, a fitting tribute to Backstrom’s legendary playmaking ability.

description:
Nominated as a finalist for the Calder Trophy as the League's best rookie, Macklin Celebrini had an outstanding first year with the San Jose Sharks. The 2024 first overall pick showcased the incredible skill set that made him the top choice the previous summer.  
One of his standout moments came in Vancouver, where he unleashed a laser-like shot with pinpoint accuracy, going bar down on the short side and beating the goalie’s glove for his 25th goal of the season—his final tally. Celebrini finished the year with 63 points, tied for second among rookies despite playing fewer games. His impressive 0.90 points per game led all rookies with more than a handful of games played, further cementing his place as one of the most exciting young talents in the League.

description:
In a crucial late-season game in April, the Montreal Canadiens fought fiercely for the final wild card spot, aiming for their first playoff berth since 2021. Trailing by a goal with seconds left against the defending Stanley Cup champions, captain Nick Suzuki stepped up, scoring the game-tying goal with just nine seconds on the clock to force overtime. In the extra period, Suzuki struck again, sealing the win with a wraparound goal and securing two critical points, leaving the Montreal crowd ecstatic.
